g.text: When RGB clipping erases an entire shading pattern
Valid Display P3 reds: R = 0.92 … 1.00, G ≤ 0.22, B ≤ 0.14
The broad light/dark shape runs from a darker pure red to a lighter red
that carries the little green and blue this corner allows.
In linear sRGB every pixel has R > 1, G < 0, B < 0.
Clipping all three channels therefore makes every pixel (1, 0, 0).
Decoded SIXEL lightness as gray: black/white = darkest/lightest source pixel (diagnostic, not color)

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #475569

g.text: Color previews: sRGB, no contrast enhancement. Gray panels: normalized diagnostics, not the original color.
